questions.question: What was the child sex-ratio as per Census 2011 of India?

• The child sex-ratio as per Census 2011 of India is **919 females per 1000 males**.

• India's child sex-ratio has been a matter of concern due to the preference for male children in various parts of the country.
 
• The government has implemented several schemes and policies to address the imbalance and improve the status of the girl child.

• The Census data is crucial for planning and policy-making at various levels of government.
 
• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of the country since 1872.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first and longest serving Attorney General of India?

questions.question: Which of the following parts of an email is used to indicate the details of the sender and recipient, as well as the date and time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Email header**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **email header** is used to indicate the details of the sender and recipient, as well as the date and time.
 
• It is a crucial part of an email that helps in identifying the source and destination of the message.
 
• Other parts of an email, such as the subject line and body, serve different purposes.
 
• The header information is typically hidden by default in most email clients but can be viewed by the user if needed.
 
• Understanding email headers can be useful for troubleshooting email delivery issues and verifying the authenticity of the message.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An email header typically includes fields like **From**, **To**, **Date**, **Subject**, and **Message-ID**.
 
• The **From** field indicates the sender's email address.
 
• The **To** field shows the recipient's email address.
 
• The **Date** field shows the date and time when the email was sent.
 
• The **Message-ID** is a unique identifier for the email message.
 
• Some email headers may also include additional information such as **Received** paths, **Reply-To** addresses, and **Return-Path** information.
 
• Analyzing email headers can help in identifying spam or phishing emails by tracing the path the email took from the sender to the recipient.

questions.question: What effect does ocean acidification have on coral reefs and shell-forming organisms?

options.text: Ocean acidification has no effect on coral reefs.
Ocean acidification weakens coral skeletons and affects reef formation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ocean acidification weakens coral skeletons and affects reef formation.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ocean acidification weakens coral skeletons and affects reef formation.**
 
• Ocean acidification is caused by the absorption of excess atmospheric CO₂ by the ocean, leading to a decrease in pH levels.
 
• This reduction in pH affects the availability of carbonate ions, which are crucial for the formation of calcium carbonate structures in corals and shell-forming organisms.
 
• As a result, corals and shell-forming organisms find it harder to construct their skeletons and shells, making them more vulnerable to damage and erosion.
 
• Weaker coral skeletons lead to less robust reef structures, impacting the biodiversity and ecological balance of reef ecosystems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coral reefs** are vital marine ecosystems that provide habitat and shelter for many marine organisms.
 
• They also protect coastlines from the damaging effects of wave action and tropical storms.
 
• Ocean acidification, along with other stressors like rising sea temperatures and pollution, poses a significant threat to the health and sustainability of coral reefs worldwide.
 
• Conservation efforts and reducing CO₂ emissions are crucial to mitigate the impact of ocean acidification on these important ecosystems.

questions.question: Which of the following princely states was taken over by the East India Company in the year 1852 AD under the principle of Whatchaap (Hadap Policy)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Udaipur.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Udaipur **was taken over by the East India Company in the year 1852 AD under the principle of Whatchaap (Hadap Policy).
 
• The Whatchaap or Hadap Policy was a doctrine applied by the British to annex Indian princely states that were either misgoverned or had no legitimate heir to the throne.
 
• This policy was part of the British strategy to expand their control in India.
 
• Sambalpur was one of the key regions affected by this policy during the mid-19th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Doctrine of Lapse** was another policy implemented by the British, where if a ruler died without a male heir, the state would be annexed.
 
• Lord Dalhousie, the Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856, was a key proponent of these annexation policies.
 
• Other states annexed under similar policies included Satara, Jhansi, and Nagpur.
 
• These policies contributed significantly to the expansion of British territories in India, leading to increased dissatisfaction and eventually the Revolt of 1857.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a part of the Directive Principles of State Policy of the Constitution of India?

options.text: Protection and improvement of environment and protection of forests and wild life.
Protection of monuments and places and objects of national importance
The provision of early childhood care and education for children under the age of six.
Provision for protection of minority areas in Rajasthan

questions.solution:

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. These principles are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• **Protection and improvement of environment and protection of forests and wild life,** is covered under Article 48A of the Directive Principles.
 
• **Protection of monuments and places and objects of national importance** is included under Article 49.

• They aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.

questions.question: Which organelle is the energy factory of the cell and an important center for intracellular interactions with other organelles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria** are the energy factories of the cell.
 
• They play a crucial role in producing ATP through the process of oxidative phosphorylation.
 
• Mitochondria are also important centers for intracellular interactions with other organelles.
 
• They have their own DNA and can replicate independently within the cell.
 
• Besides energy production, mitochondria are involved in other essential cellular processes such as signaling, cellular differentiation, and apoptosis (programmed cell death).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Golgi apparatus** is involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles.
 
• **Peroxisomes** play a key role in the metabolism of fatty acids and the detoxification of harmful substances.
 
• **Lysosomes** are involved in breaking down waste materials and cellular debris.
 
• Mitochondria are unique among organelles because they have a double membrane and their own genetic material, similar to bacteria.
 
• The endosymbiotic theory suggests that mitochondria originated from ancient bacteria that formed a symbiotic relationship with early eukaryotic cells.

questions.question:
By what other names is parliamentary government also known?

1: Cabinet Government

2: Responsive Government

3: Westminster Model of Government

4: Fixed Executive System of Government
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2 and 3 only **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Parliamentary government is also known as **Cabinet Government**, **Responsive Government**, and the **Westminster Model of Government**.
 
• These terms refer to a system where the executive branch derives its legitimacy from and is accountable to the legislature (parliament), and the head of state is different from the head of government.
 
• The **Westminster Model** is named after the Palace of Westminster, the seat of the Parliament of the United Kingdom, and is the system of government used in the UK and many of its former colonies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The key feature of parliamentary systems is the fusion of powers between the executive and legislative branches.
 
• In a parliamentary system, the executive is typically split between a head of state and a head of government.
 
• The head of government is usually the prime minister, who is appointed by the parliament.
 
• This system contrasts with a presidential system, where the executive branch is separate from the legislature.
 
• Countries that follow the Westminster Model include Canada, Australia, India, and New Zealand.

questions.question:
Calculate personal income from the following data.

I. National Income = ₹ 1,000

II. Corporate tax = ₹ 10

III. Subsidy = ₹ 5

IV. Undistributed profit = ₹ 15

V. Rent= ₹ 15
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹ 980**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **₹ 980** is the calculated personal income based on the given data.
 
• Personal Income is calculated using the formula:
 
 
• Personal Income = National Income - Corporate Tax - Undistributed Profits + Subsidies
 
 
 
• Given the values:
 
 
• National Income = ₹ 1,000
 
• Corporate Tax = ₹ 10
 
• Subsidy = ₹ 5
 
• Undistributed Profit = ₹ 15
 
 
 
• Substituting the values into the formula:
 
 
• Personal Income = ₹ 1,000 - ₹ 10 - ₹ 15 + ₹ 5
 
• Personal Income = ₹ 980
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **₹ 980**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Personal income is an important economic indicator that represents the total income received by individuals in a country from all sources, including wages, salaries, and other forms of income.
 
• It is a measure of the purchasing power of the population and can influence economic policies and decisions.
 
• Understanding personal income helps in assessing the overall economic health and standard of living of a nation.
 
• It is different from National Income, which is the total income earned by a nation's residents and businesses, including any income from abroad.

questions.question: If the atomic mass of carbon is 12.011, the atomic mass of hydrogen is 1.008 and the atomic mass of oxygen is 15.999, then calculate the molecular mass of C₂H₄O.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**44.053**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The molecular mass of a compound is calculated by summing the atomic masses of its constituent atoms.
 
• For C₂H₄O:
 
 
• Carbon (C) has an atomic mass of 12.011. Since there are 2 carbon atoms: 2 * 12.011 = 24.022
 
• Hydrogen (H) has an atomic mass of 1.008. Since there are 4 hydrogen atoms: 4 * 1.008 = 4.032
 
• Oxygen (O) has an atomic mass of 15.999. There is 1 oxygen atom: 1 * 15.999 = 15.999
 
 
 
• Summing these values gives the molecular mass of C₂H₄O: 24.022 + 4.032 + 15.999 = 44.053

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The molecular mass is a critical parameter in stoichiometry and helps in determining the proportions of elements in chemical reactions.
 
• It is also essential in calculating concentrations, determining reaction yields, and various other chemical calculations.

questions.question: Which article of the Constitution of India guarantees the right to constitutional remedies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 32** of the Constitution of India guarantees the right to constitutional remedies.
 
• This article is a fundamental right that allows individuals to move the Supreme Court (and High Courts) to seek enforcement of other fundamental rights.
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar referred to Article 32 as the "heart and soul" of the Constitution because it ensures the protection of fundamental rights.
 
• Under Article 32, the Supreme Court is empowered to issue writs, including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari, to enforce the rights.
 
• It reflects the importance placed on judicial review and the protection of individual rights within the Indian legal framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 32** is part of Part III of the Constitution, which deals with Fundamental Rights.
 
• Part III spans Articles 12 to 35, covering various rights like equality, freedom, exploitation, religion, culture, and education.
 
• Article 32 cannot be suspended except by the procedure prescribed by the Constitution, making it a critical element of the Indian judicial system.
 
• Other articles in Part III also provide specific protections, but Article 32 provides the means to enforce them.
 
• This article ensures that the judiciary acts as a guardian of the Constitution and the fundamental rights of the citizens.

questions.question: In the International System of Units (SI), the Greek letter 'Omega' is used to represent which physical quantity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electrical resistance**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electrical resistance** is represented by the Greek letter 'Omega' (Ω) in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• Resistance is a measure of the opposition to the flow of electric current in a conductor.
 
• The unit of electrical resistance is the ohm, symbolized by Ω.
 
• Ohm's Law, which states that V = IR, describes the relationship between voltage (V), current (I), and resistance (R).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Georg Simon Ohm** was the physicist who defined the law of electrical resistance, which is named after him.
 
• The concept of resistance is fundamental in electrical and electronic engineering, affecting how circuits and devices are designed and function.
 
• Materials with low resistance are called conductors, while those with high resistance are called insulators.
 
• Resistors are components specifically designed to have a certain amount of resistance, and they are used in various electronic circuits to control current flow.

questions.question: _________ overloading cannot occur.

options.text: Connecting multiple devices to a single socket
Due to sudden increase in supply voltage
Due to live wire coming in direct contact with neutral wire
By coming in contact with the live wire and the neutral wire through greater resistance.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**By coming in contact with the live wire and the neutral wire through greater resistance.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Overloading** in electrical circuits typically occurs due to **excessive current flow** which can be caused by various factors.
 
• Connecting multiple devices to a single socket can lead to **overloading** as it increases the current flow through the circuit.
 
• A sudden increase in supply voltage can cause an **overload** by pushing more current through the electrical system than it can handle.
 
• If the live wire comes in direct contact with the neutral wire, it creates a **short circuit** which can cause an overload situation.
 
• However, coming in contact with the live wire and the neutral wire through greater resistance does not cause an overload because the resistance limits the current flow, preventing an excessive amount of current from flowing through the circuit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An **overloaded circuit** is a significant safety hazard as it can lead to **overheating** and potentially cause electrical fires.
 
• Proper electrical system design and usage practices are crucial to **prevent overloading** and ensure safety.
 
• Electrical systems should be regularly inspected and maintained to avoid potential overload conditions.

• A **Community** in ecology refers to all the different species living in a particular area and interacting with each other.

• Understanding community structure and dynamics is crucial for ecological research, conservation biology, and ecosystem management.

• A **Population** is a group of individuals of the same species living in a specific area at the same time.
 
• An **Ecosystem** includes all living organisms (biotic factors) in a particular area, as well as the non-living (abiotic) components of the environment, interacting as a system.
 
• A **Habitat** is the natural environment in which a particular species lives and includes all the resources the species needs to survive, grow, and reproduce.
 
• Ecological studies often look at the relationships and interactions within communities to understand broader ecological processes.

questions.question: Who discovered the staining technique called 'Black reaction', which was capable of revealing neurons in their entirety?

• **Camillo Golgi** discovered the staining technique known as the 'Black reaction' in 1873.
 
• The 'Black reaction' or **Golgi's method** is a silver staining technique that allows for the visualization of neurons in their entirety, including their intricate structures.
 
• Golgi's method was a groundbreaking development in neuroscience, providing a way to study the detailed architecture of the nervous system.
 
• This technique was crucial in the advancement of neuroanatomy and contributed significantly to our understanding of the nervous system.
 
• Camillo Golgi was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1906** for his work on the structure of the nervous system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Camillo Golgi** was an Italian physician, pathologist, and scientist.
 
• His discovery of the Golgi apparatus, an essential cellular organelle, further cemented his legacy in the field of cell biology.
 
• The Golgi apparatus is involved in the modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins and lipids for secretion or use within the cell.
 
• Golgi's contributions laid the foundation for modern neurobiology and cellular biology, influencing numerous subsequent discoveries and advancements.

questions.question: Which of the following institutions is called 'lender of last resort'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RBI**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **RBI** (Reserve Bank of India) is known as the 'lender of last resort'.
 
• The term signifies that the RBI provides financial assistance to banks and other institutions in times of financial distress or crisis.
 
• When banks face severe liquidity issues and are unable to obtain funds from any other source, they turn to the RBI for support.
 
• RBI's role as the lender of last resort helps maintain stability in the financial system and prevents bank failures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Reserve Bank of India** was established on April 1, 1935, in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The central office of the RBI was initially established in Calcutta but was permanently moved to Mumbai in 1937.
 
• RBI regulates and supervises the financial system, manages foreign exchange, and operates the currency and credit system of the country.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the development strategy of the Government of India.
 
• RBI also acts as the banker to the Government and maintains the accounts of the central and state governments.

questions.question: Which of the following is false regarding cooking?

options.text: resulting in loss of some nutrients

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Destroys Vitamin D easily**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cooking generally **makes digestion easier** by breaking down complex food substances.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a vector quantity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mass** is a scalar quantity, which means it only has magnitude and no direction.
 
• On the other hand, **force**, **acceleration**, and **velocity** are vector quantities that have both magnitude and direction.
 
• Understanding the distinction between scalar and vector quantities is fundamental in physics as it affects how they are added, subtracted, and applied in various equations.
 
• Scalar quantities are described by a single number and units, while vector quantities require both magnitude and direction for a complete description.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In physics, **vectors** are often represented graphically by arrows, where the length of the arrow indicates the magnitude and the direction of the arrow indicates the direction of the vector.
 
• **Scalars** can be added, subtracted, multiplied, and divided like ordinary numbers, while vector operations follow specific rules, such as vector addition and vector multiplication.
 
• Common examples of scalar quantities include temperature, distance, and time, whereas common vector quantities include velocity, displacement, and electric field strength.
 
• Understanding the nature of quantities as scalar or vector is crucial in solving problems related to motion, forces, and other physical phenomena.

questions.question: In which of the following years did Sachindra Nath Sanyal establish a branch of Anushilan Samiti in Patna?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1913**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sachindra Nath Sanyal** established a branch of **Anushilan Samiti** in **Patna in 1913**.
 
• Anushilan Samiti was a prominent revolutionary organization in Bengal and played a significant role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• It was established to promote physical, mental, and spiritual development among the youth of Bengal, with a focus on achieving independence from British rule.
 
• Sachindra Nath Sanyal was a key figure in the revolutionary movement and was associated with several other revolutionary activities and organizations.
 
• The establishment of the Patna branch helped to spread the revolutionary activities and ideology of Anushilan Samiti to other parts of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anushilan Samiti** was founded by **Promotha Mitter**, **Aurobindo Ghosh**, and **Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das** in 1902.
 
• The organization was involved in several revolutionary activities, including planning and executing attacks on British officials and institutions.
 
• Sachindra Nath Sanyal later co-founded the **Hindustan Republican Association** (HRA) in 1924, which aimed to achieve independence through armed revolution.
 
• The HRA was later reorganized and renamed as the **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association** (HSRA) under the leadership of Bhagat Singh and Chandrashekhar Azad.
 
• Sanyal's contributions to the revolutionary movement were significant, and he is remembered as a prominent freedom fighter in Indian history.

questions.question: In which plant tissue does photosynthesis mainly occur?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mesophyll**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mesophyll** tissue is the primary site for photosynthesis in plants.
 
• It is located within the leaves, specifically in the palisade and spongy layers.
 
• The palisade mesophyll cells are elongated and contain numerous chloroplasts, making them highly efficient at capturing light energy.
 
• The spongy mesophyll cells have a looser arrangement, facilitating gas exchange.
 
• Photosynthesis involves the conversion of light energy into chemical energy, producing glucose and oxygen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chloroplasts** are the organelles within mesophyll cells where photosynthesis takes place.
 
• The **leaf structure** is adapted to maximize the efficiency of photosynthesis, with a large surface area and specialized cells.
 
• The **stomata** on the leaf surface control the exchange of gases, such as carbon dioxide and oxygen, which are essential for photosynthesis.
 
• Water and minerals necessary for photosynthesis are transported to the leaves through the **xylem** tissue.
 
• The **phloem** tissue distributes the produced glucose to other parts of the plant for growth and storage.
